title: Pregnancy: Self-Care, Health Care, and Risks
summary: Gaining weight is a natural part of pregnancy. Don’t try to lose weight while pregnant. While some weight gain can happen in the first trimester, it is usually small. Most of the weight gain happens in the second and third trimester. Each body is different and there is no exact amount of weight gain that you should be aiming for. summary: At least 23% of parents will experience depression or anxiety during pregnancy or after a birth. **What are the “baby blues”?** The typical mood changes that happen in the days after giving birth, affecting up to 80% of new mothers or birthing parents. title: Baby Care: Crying, Habits, Medical Care, and Safety
summary: Sometimes there’s nothing you can do to stop your baby from crying. The most important thing is to stay calm and take a break when you need it. And remember – this is a normal stage that will come to an end. When your baby won’t stop crying, it’s normal to get frustrated and angry. title: Feeding Your Baby: Breastfeeding or Chestfeeding and Expressing Milk
summary: Breastfeeding or chestfeeding offers your baby many important benefits. Human milk: The words breastfeeding and chestfeeding are used throughout this section to describe a baby being fed human milk produced by a parent at the parent’s breast or chest. You may prefer different words, like nursing. Use whichever terms you’re most comfortable with and ask that your friends, family and health care providers use them, too
